bugs.title: Electrodes are missing on the flex tail, capacitive channels are incorrectly routed capacitive buttons
bugs.description:
The eletrodes are totally missing on the capacitive flex tail. Please follow the industry standard eletrode configurations for mutual and self cap sensors. The mutual cap configuration is attached to the bug.

The cross hatch pattern is broken for CH3 and needs to be fully filled in

The shield ring for CH0-3 is too close to the cross hatch area and will need to be moved further away or removed entirely. If the shield is retained, the eletrodes for CH0-3 will need to be connected to J_FLEX using vias

The shield ring for CH3 crosses the shield ring for CH2

bugs.resolution_notes: Rewrote capacitive hatched ground offset math in local coordinate system, ensuring 100% diamond cross-hatch fill on CH3 without broken gaps. Removed inter-crossing guard rings between CH2 and CH3. Added mutual capacitive electrode interdigital pairs and self-capacitive pad electrodes routed directly to J_FLEX.

bugs.title: Source new microcontroller
bugs.description:
I want to see if a new microcontroller can be sourced for this project that'd be able to meet current and future needs:

- ARMV8m+ architecture or later (CM23 or CM33) dual core
- support for I2C, I3C, SPI, UART, PDM, external NAND flash
- includes an NPU, eGPU or DSP
- built-in NOR flash for bootloader, firmware
- SRAM or pSRAM built in for code execution
bugs.resolution_notes: Conducted architecture downselection trade study across NXP MCX N947, ST STM32U585, Renesas RA8D1, and Nordic nRF5340. Selected NXP MCX N947 (dual ARM Cortex-M33 @ 150MHz, eIQ Neutron NPU, PowerQuad DSP, 2MB dual-bank Flash, 512KB SRAM, 2x I3C, FlexSPI, 0.8mm BGA pitch). Verified 40-signal conflict-free pinmux allocation.

bugs.title: Begin downselection process
bugs.description: In order to begin the downselection process and lock this board design down, I need to look thru all the component datasheets and user manuals to provide feedback on placement and reqirements. Create a downselection report listing each component, what it does in the system architecture, and provide links to any relevant documentation for me to review. Include a pin mapping for MCU to verify that each pin connection has been made to the correct pinmux function.
bugs.resolution_notes: Created comprehensive Downselection & Architecture Report (docs/downselection_report.md) itemizing all baseline components, datasheets, reference manuals, evaluation matrix for MCU candidates (recommending NXP MCX N947 dual-core Cortex-M33 with Neutron NPU), Winbond W25N01GV NAND flash, FTDI FT232RNQ USB-UART bridge, BQ24074 charger with MAX17048 ADI fuel gauge, LP5009 I2C RGB LED driver, SWD/GPIO/peripheral headers, and verified 40-signal conflict-free MCU pinmux table.

bugs.title: Support Deep Power Down
bugs.description: Support exit from Deep Power Down when connecting the external M2 connector or charger interface
bugs.resolution_notes: Wired independent hardware wakeup triggers into MCX N947 always-on power domain: CHG_PGOOD_WAKE (TI BQ24074 /PGOOD on pin 9 to MCX N947 VBAT_WAKEUP_b ball M10 / WAKEUP0_B) and M2_WAKE_N (M.2 Key-M pin 50 PEWAKE# to MCX N947 WUU0_IN1 ball C13 / WAKEUP1_B). Both signals feature 100k pull-ups to VDD_BAT and restore PMU power upon ground assertion.

bugs.title: Verify required power on sequencing steps
bugs.description:
Verify required power on sequencing steps are performed on the test board when connecting the device to any power source:

```
• Secondary IO supplies (VDD_P2/VDD_P3/VDD_P4) must implement one of the following:
— Must be shorted with VDD (eg: single supply system), or
— Must ramp after VDD_SYS
• VDD_CORE must ramp after VDD
• VDD_P4 and VDD_ANA must be same voltage
• VDD_BAT must ramp before or with VDD_SYS
```

bugs.title: Remove manual net priorities from PCB router
bugs.description:
Replace A* router with two-stage dynamic geometric constraint scoring and rip up reroute stages:

 ### How to Eliminate Manual Net Priorities
 ┃   
 ┃   #### 1. Dynamic Geometric Constraint Sorting (Drop-in for Sequential A*)
 ┃
 ┃   Instead of matching net name strings ("I2C", "FLEX0_A", "UART0_"), net order can be
 ┃   computed dynamically from geometric degrees of freedom:
 ┃   
 ┃   • Pin Density & Depth (Escape Difficulty): Pins located deep inside dense BGA/QFN
 ┃   matrices or fine-pitch arrays have few topological escape paths (low degree of freedom).
 ┃   Computing an escape bottleneck metric automatically routes trapped inner pins first.
 ┃   • Manhattan Distance: Shorter, local point-to-point nets (such as MCU-to-adjacent-
 ┃   Flash) naturally sort ahead of long cross-board traces, preventing long-haul wires from
 ┃   cutting through local clusters.
 ┃   • Pad-to-Pad Slack: Nets with rigid placement constraints route ahead of unconstrained
 ┃   GPIOs.

 ┃   #### 3. Iterative Rip-up & Reroute (PathFinder / Negotiated Congestion)
 ┃   
 ┃   The most robust solution used by modern routers:
 ┃   
 ┃   1. Initial Overlap Routing: All nets route simultaneously or in arbitrary order on a
 ┃   cost grid, temporarily allowing overlaps/collisions.
 ┃   2. Congestion Costing: Every congested grid cell and via overlap accumulates a
 ┃   historical penalty multiplier (h_c).
 ┃   3. Rip-up and Reroute: In subsequent iterations, conflicting nets are ripped up and
 ┃   rerouted around high-congestion zones.
bugs.resolution_notes: Replaced manual net name matching in PCBAutoRouter with dynamic geometric priority scoring (pin density bottleneck, Manhattan distance, pad slack) and NetModel.priority override. Added two-stage rip-up and reroute for congested routing corridors.

bugs.title: C1 decoupling capacitor dangling without plane connections
bugs.description: C1 0402 capacitor was placed in empty space at [18.0, -21.0] without stitching vias or traces to 3V3 and GND planes.
reproduction_steps: Inspect C1 pads in kicad_pcb viewer
Verify electrical connectivity to power planes
bugs.expected_behavior: C1 must decouple U2 power pin with stitching vias to 3V3 and GND planes.
bugs.actual_behavior: C1 had isolated pads with no traces or vias connecting to copper planes.
bugs.resolution_notes: Relocated C1 to [20.0, -15.0, 0.8] opposite U2 on F.Cu. Automated plane net stitching via generation in router connected both pads to 3V3 and GND planes.

bugs.title: Piezo speaker SPK1 silkscreen border rectangular instead of round
bugs.description: SPK1 was specified with a rectangular 1x2 pin header footprint rather than a round piezo buzzer footprint, and placed far from mounting hole MH2.
reproduction_steps: Inspect SPK1 footprint shape and placement
bugs.expected_behavior: Piezo speaker must have circular silkscreen boundary and be located near mounting hole MH2.
bugs.actual_behavior: Rectangular pin header footprint rendered at [-22.0, 26.0].

attachments.description: Review screenshot requesting round piezo silkscreen

bugs.resolution_notes: Added piezo_speaker_12mm circular footprint to thru_hole.yaml, added (fp_circle ...) rendering in kicad_pcb.j2, and relocated SPK1 to [-18.0, 31.0] near MH2.

bugs.title: Collinear trace segment simplification failure in A* router due to d2[0] Y-axis typo
bugs.description: In router.py line 109, the collinear vector dot product used d2[0] instead of d2[1] for the Y-component, preventing redundant collinear waypoint pruning.
reproduction_steps: Call polyline_to_trace_segments on a 3-point collinear polyline
Observe failure to simplify into a single segment
bugs.expected_behavior: Collinear segments along X or Y axis should simplify into a single contiguous trace segment.
bugs.actual_behavior: Dot product calculation failed for vertical vectors.
bugs.resolution_notes: Fixed dot product calculation in router.py line 109: dot = d1[0] * d2[0] + d1[1] * d2[1].

bugs.title: A* router net ordering deadlock walling in local MCU control pins
bugs.description: Routing long global bus nets (PCIE, MIPI) before short local MCU escape nets (NRST, BOOT0, OSC_IN, OSC_OUT) enclosed MCU pin escapes on both F.Cu and B.Cu.
reproduction_steps: Order PCIE nets before NRST in netlist
Observe A* failure on NRST after 32 expansions
bugs.expected_behavior: Delicate local MCU escape nets must route first to secure escape corridors before long bus nets span across the board.
bugs.actual_behavior: NRST was blocked by PCIE trace on F.Cu and B.Cu.
bugs.resolution_notes: Placed MCU escape nets (OSC_IN, OSC_OUT, NRST, BOOT0) in netlist sequence immediately before PCIe bus nets. All 36 nets now route with 100% completion.

bugs.description:
The right side JST ports overlap the mating holes-J10 overlaps MH4 
J6 overlaps MH1
The right side port spacing on the carrier board and cutout spacing on the enclosure bottom needs to be revised again
bugs.resolution_notes:
Re-spaced peripheral headers J6-J10 to canonical collision-free positions with uniform 1.0 mm body gaps:
- J6 placed at Y=32.0 (length 14mm, span [25.0, 39.0]) -> top edge at Y=39.0 clears MH1 standoff (Y=37.5) and drill hole (Y=38.9); pad 1 at (24.5, 37.0) maintains 3.64mm center-to-center distance to MH1 at (25.5, 40.5) (0.59mm pad clearance, zero short).
- J7 placed at Y=17.0 (length 14mm, span [10.0, 24.0]) -> 1.0mm body gap to J6.
- J8 placed at Y=2.0 (length 14mm, span [-5.0, 9.0]) -> 1.0mm body gap to J7.
- J9 placed at Y=-14.0 (length 16mm, span [-22.0, -6.0]) -> 1.0mm body gap to J8.
- J10 placed at Y=-31.0 (length 16mm, span [-39.0, -23.0]) -> bottom edge at Y=-39.0 clears MH4 standoff (Y=-37.5) and drill hole (Y=-38.9); pad 7 at (24.5, -37.0) maintains 3.64mm center-to-center distance to MH4 at (25.5, -40.5) (0.59mm pad clearance, zero short).

Updated obstacle envelopes in `pcb.yaml`, silkscreen bus identifiers in `provider.py`, and routing stubs/vias in `routing.yaml`. Verified 0 DRC errors in KiCad and drc.py, and added regression test `test_regression_bug_179_right_side_ports_clear_mounting_holes`.

bugs.title: Resolve or suppress DRC violations
bugs.description: The carrier board and flex tail have a bunch of DRC violations. Either resolve these violations, or suppress them if they are benign/transient violations
bugs.resolution_notes:
- Added strongly-typed `rule_severities: Dict[str, str]` configuration to `PCBDesignRulesModel` in `src/model/pcb.py`, exporting to KiCad's project configuration `design_settings.rule_severities`.
- Suppressed benign and transient DRC warnings in `src/projects/carrier_board/pcb.yaml`:
  - `track_dangling: ignore`: Capacitive slider electrodes (S1-S5), action button, and proximity loop antenna traces on the flex tail are intentional open-ended capacitive sensing electrodes.
  - `hole_to_hole: ignore`: In-line breakout vias placed adjacent to PTH pads on identical electrical nets (TPs and J14).
  - `lib_footprint_issues: ignore`: Headless build environment footprint library warnings for custom test points and mounting holes.
  - `text_height: ignore`: Sub-0.8mm silkscreen reference annotations required to fit dense 0402 discrete passives and 15mm-wide flex ribbon.
  - `silk_overlap: ignore` & `silk_over_copper: ignore`: Dense component silkscreen outlines near fine-pitch pads.
  - `silk_edge_clearance: ignore`: Flex outline alignment markings near the border edge.
- Updated `src/build.py` to ensure flex PCB subassemblies inherit design rules and rule severities from project configurations.
- Verified both `carrier_board` and `flex_tail` now generate DRC reports with **0 DRC violations**, 0 unconnected pads, and 0 footprint errors.
- Added regression test `test_regression_bug_180_zero_drc_violations_carrier_board_and_flex_tail` in `src/projects/tests/test_carrier_board.py`.

bugs.title: Carrier board design hardening
bugs.description:
We have open space on the board bw J1 and J14 to harden the design:
- Add isolation jumpers bw FTDI CBUS pins for NRST and BOOT0 to design, when jumpers are removed allow the system to boot normally
- Add BOOT0 override jumper to force a boot into ISP mode during the next POR

bugs.title: Off sheet schematic feedback
bugs.description:
Feedback on the latest change to route off sheet connectors for power and ground toward the top and bottom of the sheet:
- The off sheet connectors should stop short when encountering other obstacles. In the attached screenshot, all 3 GND connectors and routing intersect with tables and component sections 
- C8 and Q1 are huge! Can we change all the discrete component formatting sot hey are sized the same as C6 on the same sheet?
- On sheet 8, pull up routing to 3V3 has stage antennas to either side of the off sheet "3V3" symbol. Screenshot attached!
- There are multiple overlaps on sheet 17. The sheet needs to be broken into multiple sub sheets (maybe 4 should work) and all of the symbol overlaps should be resolved
- Can we update the DRC engine for schematic sheets to check if text is overlapping? There is pretty prominent text overlap on this sheet. Screenshot attached
- The LED and jumper footprints on sheet 17 have overlapping text for pin labels to either side. Pins 1 and 2 for both the LED and jumper should be moved to the same side.
- The LED_AUD_K and LED_PERIPH_K text on sheet 17 is outside of the sheet border.
- On sheet 17, R7-R12 symbols are huge! please make them smaller and fix whatever is causing huge discrete components symbols to be created.
bugs.resolution_notes:
- **Obstacle Avoidance**: Constructed `obstacle_boxes` in `src/provider/schematic_diagram.py` combining component bounding boxes, title block (`202.0, 12.0, 83.0, 32.0`), decoupling card, and truth tables. Vertical GND and power trunks dynamically query obstacles and stop short with safe margins instead of cutting through tables or title blocks.
- **Discrete Component Sizing**: Standardized discrete symbol dimensions in `schematic_diagram.py`: horizontal resistor zig-zag width reduced from 20.0mm to 8.0mm (`r_half_w = 4.0`), amplitude to +/-1.6mm; capacitor plate height reduced from 15.0mm to 7.0mm (`plate_h = 3.5`), matching C6 in the decoupling capacitor bank; transistor Q1 gate and channel bars scaled down to 7.0mm and 9.0mm.
- **Pullup Stage Antennas**: Terminated pull-up vertical wire segments at `y_top_rail = y_zz_top + 6.0` in `src/provider/schematic/passives.py`, matching the horizontal crossbar and eliminating top rail overshoot stubs.
- **Sheet 17 Sub-Sheet Split**: Replaced dense single sheet with 4 clean sub-sheets in `pcb.yaml`:
  - Sheet 17: Status and Overrides - MCU Reset & Bootloader (SW1, JP1, JP2)
  - Sheet 18: Status and Overrides - Power Isolation & Boot Mode (JP3, JP4)
  - Sheet 19: Status and Overrides - Primary Power LEDs (D2, D3, D4, R7, R8, R9)
  - Sheet 20: Status and Overrides - Peripheral & MCU LEDs (D5, D6, D7, R10, R11, R12)
- **Pin Side Configuration**: Configured `pin_sides: {'1': left, '2': left}` for JP1-JP4 and D2-D7, eliminating right-side pin collisions between adjacent components.
- **Schematic DRC Text Overlap Check**: Added `compute_text_bounding_boxes` to `SchematicBoundingBoxCalculator` and `SchematicDiagram`, and integrated `SCHEMATIC_TEXT_COLLISION` and `SCHEMATIC_PAGE_BOUNDARY_EXCEEDED` checks in `PCBDesignRulesChecker.check_schematic`.
- **Wire Routing in Same-Column**: Updated `SchematicWireSegmentPlanner` in `src/provider/schematic/wire_router.py` to route collinear vertical connections directly without redundant loopbacks.
- **Regression Unit Test**: Added `test_regression_bug_206_off_sheet_schematic_feedback` in `src/tests/test_pcb_advanced.py`.

bugs.title: Remove PCIe end connector, add support for BTLE
bugs.description:
-Remove the PCIe connector and cutout from the design, there is no use case for it.
-Add support for BTLE to function as a UART connected to U1
-Minimum speed: 1Mb/s
-Support pairing by a cap touch input gesture, or proximity-based pairing (similar to AirPods)
-Antennae should be built into PCB, an external antenna is acceptable if required by design constraints. If we are adding an external antenna, the enclosure needs to be modified with an antenna mount
-Main user LED and piezo buzzer will provide the BTLE connection status information
-Bluetooth logo should be visible on the enclosure cover
-Ensure PCI and schematic design is updated
bugs.resolution_notes: Removed PCIe J1 connector and enclosure cutouts; integrated u-blox NINA-B302 U11 BTLE module with 1Mb/s UART interface, capacitive touch pairing, status LED/buzzer signaling, Bluetooth runic logo on enclosure lid, complete PCB/schematic integration, updated downselection reports and carrier board documentation, and pruned dead M.2 settings.

Resolved CSS syntax truncation where the missing brace caused subsequent rules (including modal overlay `.quake-modal-overlay` with `display: none; position: fixed`) to be ignored by browser CSS parsers, rendering modal commit dialogue elements inline at the bottom of the page with unstyled fonts.

bugs.title: Bugs reopened after clicking "Save and Exit" in dashboard
bugs.description: I clicked "Save and Exit" in the dashboard and a bunch of extra bugs appeared. I am not sure why, see the tracebacks below.
bugs.resolution_notes:
1. Started background file watcher thread unconditionally in `BugReportServer.__init__` so embedded bug server in `DashboardServer` actively detects changes in `feedback/`.
2. Fixed `/api/version` in `DashboardServer` to return the integer `db_version` counter so client-side `pollForExternalUpdates()` detects changes, and updated `/api/next_bug_id` to return `{"next_id": ...}` matching client expectations.
3. Added file watch checks to `save_and_sync()`, `/api/exit`, and mutating requests in `do_POST` so changes on disk are merged before saving.
4. Protected `RESOLVED` bug states from regressions across `merge_databases()`, `scan_and_sync_feedback_dir()`, `_handle_save_bug()`, and `export_individual_bug()`, preventing unrefreshed UI form submissions or stale markdown exports from wiping resolution notes or reopening issues.
5. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_216_save_and_exit_preserves_resolved_bugs` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

bugs.title: Add horizontal and vertical resizes to bug report page
bugs.description: Add horizontal and vertical resizers to text controls in the bug report page, and automatically increase the vertical size (up to a limit) of text controls as more information is filled in.
bugs.resolution_notes:
1. Added `resize: both !important;` to all `textarea` elements in `src/provider/templates/bug_report.html.j2`, with `min-width: 200px` and `max-width: 100%`, enabling bidirectional manual resizing.
2. Added `resize: horizontal;` to `input[type="text"]` elements with `min-width: 150px` and `max-width: 100%`.
3. Implemented `autoResizeTextarea(el, maxLimit=500)` in client-side JavaScript, calculating scroll height and dynamically adjusting element height up to a 500px limit, switching to scroll overflow when exceeding the ceiling.
4. Hooked global `input` event listener to dynamically expand textareas as information is entered, and hooked `loadActiveBug()`, `init()`, and `toggleExpandPanel()` to automatically adjust heights upon bug selection.
5. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_217_textarea_bidirectional_and_autoresize` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

bugs.title: Error creating PR
bugs.description: When I try to create a PR for the commit 4bc4bf09 I get the associated error in "Execution Logs and Tracebacks". If a PR already merged the commit into the tracking branch, can we hide the commit in the VCS window by default?
bugs.resolution_notes:
1. Updated `GitEngine.create_prs_for_commits` in `src/provider/vcs/git_engine.py` to use `git branch -a --points-at <commit>` instead of `--contains`, preventing ancestor commits from false-positive conflict detections with PR branches pointing to descendant commits.
2. Added detection of upstream tracking branch (`@{upstream}`, `origin/main`, `main`) in `GitEngine.get_smartlog_dag` and flagged merged commits using `is_merged` and `is_merged_into_tracking` fields on `CommitNodeModel`.
3. Updated PR creation to cleanly reject attempts to create PRs for commits already merged into the tracking branch.
4. Added `#smartlogList.hide-merged` styling and default hidden state in `src/provider/templates/diff_view.html.j2`, tagging merged nodes with `.merged-commit` and adding a `✓ Merged` badge (`.node-badge-merged`).
5. Added `btnToggleMerged` button in the Smartlog header with localStorage persistence (`diffview_hide_merged`) allowing users to toggle merged commit visibility on demand.
6. Added automated regression test `test_regression_bug_218_pr_creation_points_at_and_merged_commits_hidden` in `src/tests/test_dashboard.py`.

bugs.title: Unexpected isolation results in flying probes test
bugs.description: Flying probes test- there's a bunch of isolation test results that are included for the flex tail that shouldn't be possible to test. Pasted into Tracebacks section below
bugs.resolution_notes:
1. Updated `verify_signal_lines_isolation` in `src/provider/simulation/flying_probe.py` to accept `subassembly: Optional[str] = None` and return empty isolation checks when inspecting `flex_tail`, as the flexible tail lacks opposing test pads or local DC power/ground reference test points for galvanic isolation probing.
2. Updated `create_flying_probe_hooks` in `src/provider/simulation/flying_probe.py` to pass `subassembly=target_label` and filter `board_comp_names` so that `flex_tail` simulation only loads test steps explicitly defined for `flex_tail` in `pcb_test_steps.yaml` (7 capacitive and continuity steps), omitting nonexistent `TEST_ISO_*` steps.
3. Verified `render_markdown_test_report` omits the `Signal Line Isolation Audit` section when `isolation_checks` is empty, while correctly rendering `Mutual Capacitance Touch Simulation & Verification (Flex Tail)`.
4. Added automated regression unit test `test_regression_bug_220_flex_tail_flying_probe_isolation_excluded` in `src/projects/tests/test_carrier_board.py`.

```
# 1. Store the stash's commit hash into a variable
STASH_HASH=$(git rev-parse stash@{0})

# 2. Pop the stash to bring your files back into your working directory
git stash pop

# 3. Rename the file using the stored hash
mv CR_feedback.md "CR_${STASH_HASH}.md"

# 4. Amend renamed feedback file
git commit -a
```

bugs.title: Add sort and filter menus to Bug Report field

bugs.title: NINA-VLOAD_SW pin not in the documentation
bugs.description: Sheet 2 shows a Q1 transistor going to a VLOAD_SW on the NINA. VLOAD_SW has no pin marker, and there is no VLOAD_SW in the NINA docs. I think this is an artifact of when the PCIe express connector was populated. Can we remove it and correct the BLE module footprint and pinout? We can use modem commands to power on or off the NINA; no need for a separate GPIO
bugs.resolution_notes: Removed legacy VLOAD_SW net, pruned VLOAD_SW from U11 pin breakouts and Sheet 2, connected U11 VCC directly to 3V3 system rail, corrected NINA pin 18 from VLOAD_SW to SWITCH_2 in ic.yaml, and pruned VLOAD_SW traces and vias from routing.yaml.

bugs.title: NINA-Utilize Native nRF52840 NFC on the NINA-B312
bugs.description:
┃   The u-blox NINA-B312 module is based on the Nordic Semiconductor nRF52840 SoC, which features an
 ┃   integrated NFC-A Type 2 / Type 4 Tag peripheral with hardware touch-to-wake support.
 ┃ 
 ┃   • Hardware Requirements:
 ┃       • Route the NFC1 and NFC2 pins from the NINA-B312 module footprint to an external 13.56 MHz tuned coil
 ┃       antenna.
 ┃       • Place two external tuning shunt capacitors (C_{tune1}, C_{tune2}, typically 180--330 pF NPO/C0G)
 ┃       across NFC1/NFC2 to match the target antenna loop inductance to resonance at 13.56 MHz (f =
 ┃       1/(2π√(L_{ant}C_{tot}))).
 ┃   • Pros: Zero additional active ICs, zero added quiescent current, and native Nordic SDK / Zephyr / Embassy
 ┃   firmware driver support.
bugs.resolution_notes: Routed native nRF52840 NFC1/NFC2 from U11 (NINA-B312) to external tuned coil antenna header J16 with 300pF C0G shunt tuning capacitors C18 and C19, achieving 0 DRC violations.

bugs.title: NINA-Remove J15 from BOM, mark board connector as no connect
bugs.description: Remove J15 from the carrier_board BOM, and mark J15 as no connect in the schema. Connect RESET_N on U11 to a push button switch adjacent to J15.
bugs.resolution_notes: Marked J15 as DNP and no-connect, excluded from BOM export and schematic unconnected DRC checks, wired U11 RESET_N to push button switch SW2 adjacent to J15 with zero DRC violations.

bugs.title: Carrier board schematic feedback-floating pins, component spacing, off sheet connectors
bugs.description:
Sheet 3: BYP on U10 shows up as floating
Sheet 4: Pin D1 on U1 shows up as floating
Sheet 8: VREGD and VREGA- off sheet connectors placed here, but not used elsewhere in the sheet?
Sheet 10: EGP/GND on U11 shows up as floating
Sheet 11: J15 and SW2- can we move them to the middle of the sheet?
Can we remove these unused pins from the schematic or route them appropriately, and address all other schematic formatting issues
bugs.resolution_notes: Resolved floating pins on U10 (BYP) and U1 (D1) by removing unused pins from Sheet 3 and 4 breakouts. Removed dangling off-sheet connectors for VREGD and VREGA on Sheet 8 U2, added *VREG* to POWER_NET_PATTERNS and grouped decoupling caps by power net to prevent cross-rail bridging. Refined allowed_pins matching in schematic diagram and DRC to prevent false label matching of secondary ground pins (EGP, GND_12, GND_26, GND_30) on U11. Updated cols_override layout spacing to honor col_gap and center components horizontally and vertically on Sheet 11 (J15, SW2).

bugs.title: Supplier PCB guidelines
bugs.description:
Each project should output supplier files:
-gerbers.zip: contains .pcb .pcbdoc .cam .brd and gerber files
-bom_templates.zip: contains <PCB name>_bom.csv BOM list for each PCB
-centroid_files.zip: contains <PCB name>_pos.csv centroid list for each PCB
-assembly_files.zip: contains <PCB name>_top.png, <PCB name>_bottom.png top and bottom PCB textures for each PCB
The zip files should go under build/board
bugs.resolution_notes: Added Builder.package_supplier_pcb_files to automatically package supplier zip archives under build/board and build/board/<project>: gerbers.zip (contains .pcb, .pcbdoc, .cam, .brd, and all gerber files), bom_templates.zip (contains <PCB name>_bom.csv for each PCB), centroid_files.zip (contains <PCB name>_pos.csv for each PCB), and assembly_files.zip (contains <PCB name>_top.png and <PCB name>_bottom.png textures for each PCB). Added regression test test_regression_bug_262_supplier_pcb_guidelines_zip_outputs.

bugs.title: Simplify build logging
bugs.description:
Can we simplify the logging of tools long these lines-
-Only log what target got built to stdout
-Use structured logging to log individual file compilations to build/daemon.log
Example below

We could extrapolate this further to all tools. For example, in the new scheme view.py should only show the target being shown, and everything else would be output to daemon.log:

$ python src/view.py carrier_board/carrier_board:pcb
👁️ Showing carrier_board_carrier_board_pcb 
▶ + 
✔ Done Visualizing...

$ python src/view.py carrier_board/carrier_board:pcb
👁️ Showing carrier_board_carrier_board_pcb 
✔ Done Visualizing...
bugs.expected_behavior: $ python src/build.py "carrier_board/*"
bugs.actual_behavior: $ python src/build.py "carrier_board/*"
bugs.resolution_notes: Route individual file compilation logs to build/daemon.log via Logger.log structured logging, keeping stdout clean with only target compilation summaries and completion status.

bugs.title: Remove component designators for LEDs and jumpers
bugs.description: Component designators for LEDs and jumpers are on the opposite of where the components are placed. This has no functional purpose-we can remove all these designators
bugs.resolution_notes: Remove opposite-side component designators D2..D7, R7..R12, JP1..JP4, and SW1 from bottom silkscreen (B.SilkS) in CarrierBoardProvider.silkscreen().

bugs.title: C18 and C19-too close to U11
bugs.description: Can we move C18 and C19 further away from U11 and stack them vertically? Right now, C18 is inside the silkscreen border of U11
bugs.resolution_notes: Moved C18 and C19 to X=7.0 stacked vertically outside U11 silkscreen border; updated NFC1, NFC2, and GND traces and vias; added regression unit test test_regression_bug_267_c18_c19_vertical_stack_and_u11_clearance

bugs.title: I seem to have to rebuilt the carrier_board project to view PCB changes
bugs.description: This seems like a general build issue, but it repress easily for the carrier_board project. I need to rebuild the carrier_board project to view PCB changes. I placed example commands in expected/actual showing what command I want to run to view the updated PCB and what I actually have to run
bugs.expected_behavior: $ python src/view.py carrier_board/carrier_board:pcb
bugs.actual_behavior: $ python src/build.py "carrier_board/*"
bugs.resolution_notes: Propagate all PCB configuration models (omitted_silkscreen_designators, silkscreen_graphics, design_rules, net_classes, schematic_sheets, revision) to pcb_cfg in view.py and target_cfg in build.py, ensuring view.py immediately exports and displays the latest PCB changes without requiring build.py first.

bugs.title: encode LFS attachments in a way that multiple bugs can have an attachment with the same name
bugs.resolution_notes: Encode attachments scoped by bug ID under attachments/<bug_id>/<filename>, preventing collisions when multiple bugs share identical attachment filenames while maintaining Git LFS tracking and HTTP serving.

bugs.title: Remediations for stuck CI tasks
bugs.description:
We need to implement the following remediations for stuck CI tasks:

  ### Recommended Remediation

  #### A. Terminate the Build Daemon in ci-gate.yml or Pass --no-daemon

  To prevent orphan daemon processes from keeping the runner host alive, ensure the daemon is cleanly stopped or bypassed in CI:

          - name: Run Smoke Tests
            shell: bash -el {0}
            env:
              PYTHONPATH: src
            run: |
              set -o pipefail
              python src/smoke.py
              python src/daemon.py stop || true

  Alternatively, in smoke.py:37-41, automatically append --no-daemon when executing build.py or view.py so no background processes
  are spawned.

  #### B. Add a SIGTERM Handler to daemon.py

  Register signal handlers so daemon.py exits immediately when the runner sends SIGTERM:

    import signal

    def handle_sigterm(signum, frame):
        sys.exit(0)

    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, handle_sigterm)

  #### C. Add Concurrency & Missing Event Triggers to ci-gate.yml

  Update the top of .github/workflows/ci-gate.yml:

    name: CI Gate Validation
    on:
      pull_request:
        types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]

    concurrency:
      group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
      cancel-in-progress: true
bugs.resolution_notes: Implemented concurrency cancellation and ready_for_review triggers in ci-gate.yml, added --no-daemon auto-injection in smoke.py, and added SIGTERM graceful shutdown in daemon.py

bugs.title: Create motor hub assembly
bugs.description:
Right now debugging motor issues is very difficult. Can we pls create a motor hub assembly which combines the hall sensor, motor, drive hub, and motor clip into a single subassembly unit which clips into the bottom of the bowl and interfaces magnetically with the impeller? See this additional feedback for more optimizations and improvements:

1. Center the Thrust Bearing (Reduce Friction Radius by 90%):
      • Remove the outer perimeter standoff ring on the drive hub at R = 15.6 mm.
      • Add a small PTFE (Teflon) thrust washer or tiny acetal/POM button directly around the 1.5 mm motor shaft collar at R ≤ 1.5
      mm.
      • Dropping the contact radius from 15.6 mm down to 1.5 mm reduces friction torque by over 90% (T_f ∝ R).

2. Optimize Magnetic Coupling Strength:
      • Increase the axial air gap from 1.5 mm to 2.0--2.5 mm. Magnetic attraction drops with 1/d² while rotational
      magnetic coupling torque remains sufficient for fluid pumping.

3. Speed Sensor Pocket Alignment:
      • Ensure that the Hall sensor pocket at Y = 18.5 mm directly aligns with the drive hub's magnet pitch circle so the Hall
      sensor receives strong alternating pulses to reliably output SPEED_SENSE (GP26). 
      • These are the hall sensors I purchased: 

https://www.amazon.com/FORIOT-Effect-Sensor-3144E-A3144/dp/B0H69BSJ4Z/ref=sr_1_4_pp?crid=ZUG52D2UM8C&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.lpKwwD9zXT4MytW_o1867YiT79Yl-lsXrO86wfgsgnShDxXo1Ptvdg432J9RLfUlPqg3sgQwgI4ajloN9FG2Zlo3KyUWIIIhG1epfbhZ8rnOzwoVy8yOpe6GIQNE5Si866q-1S70Y6wKyFPuvuxLJ8Qlbu4LJdNtf5Sjqjq45d-qswe8QjFcGbVlpS3Cpaxq770C7UN_pKv_ssgpbkmEzIl_EmazNDYryvgi4d-H-38.jt36wv_LPOYxzl2HI64T4n84lfvUbY3Z5gwIZfFs2bI&dib_tag=se&keywords=hall+sensor&qid=1792796296&sprefix=hall+senso%2Caps%2C183&sr=8-4
